note: An experiment (GAME_SPEC §13.7, Stage 44) on data/benches/precipitate.json: a precipitate. Sodium hydroxide poured into copper sulfate brings the copper out as pale blue copper hydroxide (a fast equilibrium, Ksp about 4e-20); boiled down, the hydroxide gives up its water and turns black (Fukuda's rate: slow under water, seconds once dry and above 150 C); acid dissolves the oxide, blue again (chem_tool study precipitation).
title: Experiment: a precipitate

steps.title: A little base into the copper sulfate
steps.text: Pick up the base bottle, then right-click the beaker. Drag the menu's slider to about 10 mL, then click "pour". Point at the beaker to read what it holds.
steps.why: The beaker holds blue copper sulfate: copper ions, Cu2+, in water. The base brings hydroxide ions, OH-. Together they make copper hydroxide, Cu(OH)2, which hardly dissolves at all: it comes out of the solution at once as a pale blue powder, a precipitate.

steps.title: Base to spare
steps.text: Pick up the base again, right-click the beaker, slide to about 15 mL and pour.
steps.why: Each copper ion takes two hydroxide ions: 20 mL of the base brings out all 0.01 mol of the copper. Past that the base is left over, the pH leaps, and the liquid is clear: the blue was the copper ions, and they are in the powder now.

steps.title: A burner under it
steps.text: Pick up the burner in the cabinet, then click the beaker.
steps.why: Copper hydroxide holds its water less firmly than it seems: it is less stable than copper oxide and water, and only slow to change.

checks.text: the burner is under the beaker

steps.title: Full flame
steps.text: Right-click the burner to choose it, then drag its valve fully open. Then click 60x on the clock to hurry the wait.
steps.why: Under boiling water half of the hydroxide turns in about half an hour (Ea 127 kJ/mol). Once the water has boiled away and it is hotter, above 150 C, it takes seconds.

steps.title: It turns black
steps.text: Watch the beaker: the water boils away, and the pale blue powder darkens to black.
steps.why: Cu(OH)2 -> CuO + H2O: the water leaves as steam, and black copper oxide stays, the same oxide the demo makes from malachite.

steps.title: Flame off
steps.text: Right-click the burner, then drag its valve shut. Wait for the beaker to cool below 40 C.
steps.why: Acid on a hot, dry beaker would spit as it boiled.

steps.title: Acid on the oxide
steps.text: Pick up the acid bottle, right-click the beaker, slide to about 20 mL and pour. Watch the black powder.
steps.why: The acid first neutralises the base left over, then eats the oxide: CuO + H2SO4 -> CuSO4 + H2O. The copper is dissolved and blue again; the 0.01 mol went round a cycle and none of it was lost.

checks.text: about 20 mL of acid in the beaker

goal.text: every element, mass and energy unchanged

results.label: the copper sulfate at the end
